title: Solar flare ribbon areas: space-filling territory or fractal area
status: Specified and committed BEFORE the ribbon data were obtained or inspected. The data host was not reachable from the registering environment; the analysis script experiments/run_flare_ribbons.py is ready to run where it is. The prediction was first committed in docs/resource-catalogue.md (commit e4bf526).
prior_exposure: No ribbon-area distribution from this database has been read by the registrant. If its authors or others have published a power-law index for ribbon areas, the person running the test should record whether they had read it before running.
question: Is the frequency distribution of flare ribbon areas that of a space-filling two-dimensional territory (log-orthopolic in area) or that of a fractal area?

H_territory.why: Territory rule alpha = 1 + d_s/D_k with support dimension d_s = 2 (the chromospheric surface tiled by ribbon footprints) and area ∝ L^2 (D_k = 2): equal ribbon area per logarithmic area class.

H_fractal.why: Fractal-diffusive self-organized criticality (Aschwanden): N(L) ∝ L^-3 with fractal area A ∝ L^(3/2) gives alpha_A = 1 + 2/(3/2) = 7/3.

hypotheses.note: The two hypotheses agree on the distribution of linear sizes, N(L) ∝ L^-3. They differ only in how measured area scales with size, so this test discriminates a space-filling from a fractal area, which is the distinction the orthopolic territory reading makes.

data.source: RibbonDB: Kazachenko, M. D., Lynch, B. J., Welsch, B. T. and Sun, X. (2017), A database of flare ribbon properties from the Solar Dynamics Observatory. I. Reconnection flux, Astrophysical Journal 845, 49. Reported host: http://solarmuri.ssl.berkeley.edu/~kazachenko/RibbonDB/ (verify; about 3,000 flares of GOES class C1.0 and above, 2010-2016).
data.variable: Total (cumulative) ribbon area per flare, as tabulated; secondary: ribbon reconnection flux.
data.input_format: CSV with one row per flare and a positive numeric column named by --column.

estimator.model: Continuous power law above x_min, maximum likelihood (Clauset, Shalizi and Newman 2009).
estimator.x_min: Minimum Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance over candidate quantiles 0.30-0.90 of the data (GOES-class selection makes small ribbons incomplete).
estimator.uncertainty: Percentile 95% interval from 2,000 bootstrap resamples of flares (seed 20261008), refitting x_min in each.
estimator.goodness_of_fit: Parametric bootstrap KS p-value (500 replicates); lognormal likelihood-ratio comparison reported.

decision_rule.inconclusive: Interval contains both or neither, or the power law is rejected at p <= 0.1.

secondary: Repeat for reconnection flux; under a size-independent mean field strength the same hypotheses apply.
